# Narcolepsy Authorization Guide
_Decision Support_

Specialty: Sleep Medicine
Logo URL: /manus-storage/narcolepsy-compass-logo_980d50d6.png
Appeal letter action navigates to: /sleep/narcolepsy/appeal-letter

## CPT Codes — Narcolepsy Workup & Management

| CPT Code | Description | Auth Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 95810 | Polysomnography (PSG) — ≥6 parameters, attended | Often | Required before MSLT per AASM |
| 95805 | Multiple Sleep Latency Test (MSLT) | Often | Must follow PSG; 5 nap opportunities |
| 95806 | Sleep study, unattended, Type III | Sometimes | Not appropriate for narcolepsy workup |
| 99213–99215 | Office visit — E&M (sleep specialist) | Rarely | Document EDS, cataplexy, ESS score |
| G0399 | Home sleep apnea test (Type III) | Rarely | Not diagnostic for narcolepsy |

## ICD-10-CM Diagnosis Codes

| ICD-10 | Description | Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G47.411 | Narcolepsy with cataplexy (Type 1) | Cataplexy confirmed; CSF hypocretin low or absent |
| G47.419 | Narcolepsy without cataplexy (Type 2) | EDS + MSLT positive; no cataplexy; normal CSF |
| G47.421 | Narcolepsy in conditions classified elsewhere, with cataplexy | Secondary narcolepsy with cataplexy |
| G47.429 | Narcolepsy in conditions classified elsewhere, without cataplexy | Secondary narcolepsy without cataplexy |
| G47.10 | Hypersomnia, unspecified | Pending full diagnostic workup |
| G47.19 | Other hypersomnia | Idiopathic hypersomnia, Kleine-Levin |

## Medication Prior Authorization Requirements

### Sodium Oxybate (Xyrem)
Brand: Xyrem / Jazz Pharmaceuticals
Schedule: Schedule III (REMS program required)
Requirements:
- Confirmed narcolepsy diagnosis (PSG + MSLT)
- DEA Schedule III — REMS enrollment mandatory
- Prescriber must be REMS-certified
- Pharmacy: Certified specialty pharmacy only
- Step therapy: Modafinil or stimulant trial often required first
Common denial reason: REMS non-compliance, step therapy not met

### Low-Sodium Oxybate (Lumryz)
Brand: Lumryz / Avadel
Schedule: Schedule III (REMS program required)
Requirements:
- Same as Xyrem; once-nightly formulation
- REMS enrollment required
- Step therapy: Prior Xyrem or stimulant trial
Common denial reason: Step therapy, formulary preference for Xyrem

### Pitolisant (Wakix)
Brand: Wakix / Harmony Biosciences
Schedule: Non-scheduled (H3 receptor antagonist)
Requirements:
- Confirmed narcolepsy diagnosis
- PSG + MSLT documentation
- Step therapy: Modafinil trial often required
- Preferred for patients with substance use risk
Common denial reason: Step therapy not met, off-label use for Type 2

### Solriamfetol (Sunosi)
Brand: Sunosi / Jazz Pharmaceuticals
Schedule: Schedule IV
Requirements:
- Confirmed narcolepsy diagnosis
- PSG + MSLT documentation
- Step therapy: Modafinil trial often required
Common denial reason: Step therapy, formulary tier restrictions

### Modafinil (Provigil) / Armodafinil (Nuvigil)
Brand: Provigil / Nuvigil (generics available)
Schedule: Schedule IV
Requirements:
- Narcolepsy diagnosis (ICD-10 G47.41x)
- Often first-line per payer step therapy
Common denial reason: Rarely denied for confirmed narcolepsy

## Documentation Checklist for Prior Auth
- PSG report with total sleep time, sleep efficiency, REM latency, and SOREMP notation
- MSLT report: mean sleep onset latency ≤8 min AND ≥2 SOREMPs
- ESS score ≥10 documented in clinic note
- Cataplexy description (if Type 1): specific emotional triggers, duration, frequency
- CSF hypocretin-1 level (if obtained): ≤110 pg/mL diagnostic for NT1
- Sleep specialist attestation of ICSD-3 diagnostic criteria
- Step therapy documentation: prior stimulant/modafinil trial with inadequate response
- REMS enrollment confirmation (for sodium oxybate)
- Absence of contraindications (e.g., MAOIs for pitolisant; severe hepatic impairment for oxybate)

## References
1. Maski K, et al. "Treatment of Central Disorders of Hypersomnolence: An American Academy of Sleep Medicine Clinical Practice Guideline." J Clin Sleep Med. 2021;17(9):1881–1893.
2. American Academy of Sleep Medicine. International Classification of Sleep Disorders, 3rd ed. Darien, IL: AASM; 2014.
3. Dauvilliers Y, et al. "Narcolepsy with cataplexy." Lancet. 2007;369(9560):499–511.
4. Thorpy MJ, et al. "Consensus practice parameters for the treatment of narcolepsy." Sleep. 2001;24(4):451–466.
5. AASM Practice Guidelines: https://aasm.org/clinical-resources/practice-standards/practice-guidelines/
